newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: U.S. job data push Dutch shares up late in session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. job data push Dutch shares up late in session.

text.p: Dutch shares ended mixed on Friday after a session which focused on the afternoon release of U.S. jobless data over April.
The market warmly welcomed the data, and most stocks edged higher after their release, although some traders said the figures were difficult to interpret.
The AEX main share index ended down 1.17 points at 771.57, but above its intra-day low of 768.24, while the AMX midcap index closed 9.58 points higher at 1183.92 points.
The U.S. jobless rate fell to 4.9 in April from 5.2 percent in March.
April jobs rose 142,000 against a forecasted 211,000 gain, while the March figure was revised to 139,000 from 175,000.
"The revised figures are often so different from the initial ones, it almost seems pointless to react to those first figures," one dealer complained.
Average hourly earnings slipped to $12.14 from $12.15, whereas market players had expected a 0.3 percent rise.
Unilever ended down 3.60 at 377.80 guilders on disappointing first quarter figures released before the opening.
The food and detergents group reported net profit of 898 million guilders, up from 808 in the first quarter of 1996.
KNP BT closed 1.10 higher at 39.50 guilders, benefiting from first quarter profit of 52 million guilders, two million guilders higher than in the year-ago period.
Analyst forecasts had ranged from 40 to 48 million guilders as the company had said it expected lower first quarter earnings barely one month ago.
"Apparently, the company is still not able to give a reliable forecast," analyst Jan Wirken of IRIS Research said.
High-tech firm Getronics continued to feel the effects of an upgrade by Morgan Stanley, which dated from two weeks ago but revived the stock on Thursday, dealers said.
"Once they read it in the paper, a lot of people still jump upon it," one dealer said. The share ended 60 cents higher at 62.30 guilders.
High-techs ASM Lithography and Cap Gemini also climbed.
Dealers said ASML and Cap Gemini probably benefited from the Nasdaq's higher close on Thursday.
The Nasdaq outpaced the Dow on Thursday, closing up, while the Dow ended lower.
Philips climbed 1.80 guilders to 108.10 in heavy trade with dealers citing a broker upgrade.
"The stock has been upgraded by Prudential Bache in the U.S.," one dealer said.
Vendex shares coast 2.80 guilders higher at end of the session, closing at 95.50 guilders. Temporary employment agency Randstad ended 4.50 higher at 180.00 guilders.
"It's a very volatile market. We're just below the all-time high and can't break it for the moment," one said.
"With the results and annual reports season almost behind us, the direction all depends upon interest and currency factors for the next couple of months," one dealer said.
